label: copy-phase input o (late), esp. when o is followed by e/o
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and 99% of activation mass is on steps whose input is the letter o (the model re-reading an o it just output). Almost never fires on other inputs (a few weak hits on e), and never in the original or delimiter phases. Being an o input is necessary but far from sufficient: only ~3% of copy-phase o inputs fire. Firing is concentrated where the next original token (current output) is e (55% of mass) or o (25%), with k and z next. It prefers later recall positions (recall_idx >= 3, near the end of the sequence; almost none at recall_idx <= 2). The strongest examples are the pattern u o e, where the input o follows u and the output is e. The predicate o-input & output in {e,o} & recall_idx >= 3 reaches dev F1 0.55 / mass recall 0.79. Precision stays near 0.5, so some unidentified context also gates it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=o (+5.85), in_tok=o (+4.00), prev_tok=u (+3.86), phase=2 & in_tok=e (+3.49), phase=2 & out_tok=e (+3.10), phase=2 & out_tok=z (+3.07).
